contradicting_evidence: Negative settled ETF flows and contraction across all supplied stablecoin-supply windows could turn an uneven repair into a more directional decline.
Positive daily returns, 66% advancing breadth and modest ETH daily outperformance could instead develop into a sustained recovery.
The available observations are too sparse to establish that alternating rebound and retest behavior is already persistent.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: Uneven rebound and retest attempts are more defensible than clean continuation. The downside has greater background pressure from flows and liquidity, but positive daily participation prevents a one-way decline call. BTC resilience alone would not establish transmission into broader altcoins.
falsification_conditions: Persistent gains in BTC and ETH, strengthening ETH/BTC and repeated improvement in broad relative participation would weaken the mixed path toward UP.
Persistent lower closes, declining participation and continuing adverse settled-flow evidence would weaken the mixed path toward DOWN.
missing_evidence: Repeated daily and intraday observations showing whether current positive participation survives subsequent price tests.
New settled ETF evidence beyond November 5.
A persistent ETH/BTC trend and canonical breadth confirmation rather than a single proxy snapshot.
supporting_evidence: Positive BTC and ETH daily returns and majority advancing breadth support the possibility of stabilization or further rebound.
The latest supplied hour moved lower in both assets, while ETF outflows and shrinking stablecoin supply challenge the durability of that rebound.
Only 36% of the breadth universe outperformed BTC and 31% outperformed ETH, so positive absolute participation is not equivalent to broad relative leadership.

Capitalization participation is uneven: the large-alt proxy had about 71% advancers, the mid-alt proxy 50%, and the Top-100-tail small-alt proxy about 71%. This is not an orderly, confirmed transmission sequence.
